subject: ent
title: Tracheostomy and airway foreign bodies

steps.tx: **Tracheostomy** opens the anterior trachea (usually second to fourth rings) to bypass upper airway obstruction, assist prolonged ventilation, or clear secretions the glottis cannot protect. Elective open tracheostomy divides strap muscles and (often) thyroid isthmus under direct vision, while **percutaneous dilatational** technique (ICU, Seldinger wire) suits ventilated selected patients. **Cricothyrotomy** through cricothyroid membrane is the emergency cannot intubate cannot oxygenate rescue (palpable landmark, quick), converted to formal tracheostomy within days because subglottic stenosis risk rises with prolonged cricothyroid cannulation.
steps.say: Tracheostomy bypasses the blocked top; cricothyrotomy is the emergency hole through the membrane, converted later.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Tube choice shapes safety: cuffed tubes seal ventilated airways and protect against aspiration, uncuffed or fenestrated tubes suit spontaneously breathing weaning patients (fenestration plus inner tube removal permits phonation and trials of capping). First tube change waits about five to seven days until a mature tract forms; earlier dislodgement collapses the track and needs senior airway hands, stay sutures and immediate reinsertion equipment at the bedside. Humidification, suction discipline, inner tube cleaning and cuff pressure monitoring (around 20 to 30 cm water) prevent mucosal injury.
steps.say: First week the track is fresh: lost tube early is an airway emergency. Cuffs seal, fenestrations talk.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Early complications strike within days: haemorrhage (including catastrophic innominate artery erosion from low placed or overinflated cuffs heralded by sentinel bleeds), surgical emphysema, pneumothorax, tube displacement or obstruction by crusts and plugs, and wound infection. Late complications include tracheal stenosis (cuff site or stoma), tracheomalacia, tracheo oesophageal or tracheo innominate fistula, persistent tracheocutaneous fistula after long term cannulation, and stomal granulation or keloid. Bleeding from a tracheostomy weeks out is fistula until proven otherwise and needs theatre, not bedside optimism.
steps.say: Sentinel bleed from a tracheostomy warns of great vessel erosion. Late stenosis and fistulae are pressure injuries.

steps.tx: **Airway foreign bodies** peak in toddlers with organic objects (peanut oils inflame and swell): sudden choking, then cough, unilateral wheeze or quiet lung, ball valve air trapping on expiratory films (normal film never excludes). Laryngeal objects threaten complete obstruction; bronchial objects migrate usually rightward. Rigid bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia with ventilation control is diagnostic and therapeutic gold standard; flexible scopes sample distally in adults. **Decannulation** follows capping tolerance by day, safe swallow, secretion control and treated cause, stepping down tube size before removal with stoma strapping and observation.
steps.say: Choked toddler, one quiet lung: rigid bronchoscopy. Decannulate only after capped days and safe swallow.
